examples.en: I pressed my clothes tightly into the bag.
You have to roll the gimbap tightly so it doesn't burst.

examples.ko: 상자 안에 책이 꽉꽉 들어차 있어요.
examples.en: The box is packed full of books.

examples.ko: 주말 아침인데 지하철이 사람으로 꽉꽉 찼어요.
examples.en: Even though it's a weekend morning, the subway was jam-packed with people.
I tie my shoelaces tight and run.
I packed the snow firmly and made a snowman.

explain: '꽉'보다 여러 번 힘을 주거나 빈틈없이 가득 채우는 느낌이 더 강해요. '꽉꽉 눌러 담다', '꽉꽉 채우다', '꽉꽉 들어차다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '꽉', it feels more emphatic, as if you press repeatedly or leave no gap at all. It often appears in set combinations such as '꽉꽉 눌러 담다', '꽉꽉 채우다' and '꽉꽉 들어차다'.

examples.en: The child was startled and let out a shriek.
The duck quacked loudly and ran away.

examples.ko: 갑자기 뒤에서 꽥 소리를 질러서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Someone suddenly yelled behind me and I was startled.

examples.ko: 동생이 화가 나서 나한테 꽥 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got angry and yelled at me.

examples.ko: 거위가 낯선 사람을 보고 꽥 울었어요.
examples.en: The goose honked sharply when it saw a stranger.

examples.ko: 아버지가 갑자기 꽥 하고 화를 내셔서 모두 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: Dad suddenly snapped angrily, and everyone went quiet.

explain: 갑자기 크고 날카롭게 나는 소리를 나타내요. '꽥 소리를 지르다', '꽥 하고 화를 내다'처럼 쓰고, 오리나 거위 소리에도 써요. 소리가 이어지면 '꽥꽥'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes a sudden, loud, sharp sound. You say '꽥 소리를 지르다' or '꽥 하고 화를 내다', and it also fits ducks and geese. For a repeated sound, use '꽥꽥'.

examples.en: The ducks quack on the pond all day long.

examples.ko: 그렇게 꽥꽥거리지 말고 차분히 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't yell like that; try speaking calmly.

examples.ko: 옆집 아이가 복도에서 꽥꽥거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The kid next door was screaming in the hallway, so I couldn't sleep.
Why are you yelling only at me since this morning?

examples.ko: 시장에서 아저씨가 꽥꽥거리며 물건을 팔고 있어요.
examples.en: A man at the market is shouting as he sells his goods.
My friend screamed when he saw his test result.

explain: 오리 소리에도 쓰지만, 사람이 시끄럽게 소리를 지를 때 쓰면 '왜 저렇게 시끄럽게 굴어' 하는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '소리치다'보다 거칠게 들리니까 남에게 직접 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요. 비슷하게 '꽥꽥대다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for ducks, but when applied to people it sounds negative, as if they are being noisy and annoying. It sounds harsher than '소리치다', so saying it directly to someone can be rude. '꽥꽥대다' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 사물놀이는 꽹과리, 장구, 북, 징 네 가지 악기로 연주해요.
examples.en: Samulnori is played with four instruments: the kkwaenggwari, janggu, buk and jing.

examples.ko: 사물놀이 동아리에서 한 학기 동안 꽹과리를 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned the kkwaenggwari for a semester in the samulnori club.

examples.ko: 꽹과리 소리가 크고 높아서 멀리서도 들려요.
examples.en: The kkwaenggwari sounds loud and high, so you can hear it from far away.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 꽹과리를 치면 모두 춤을 춰요.
examples.en: When Grandpa plays the kkwaenggwari, everyone dances.

examples.ko: 축제 날 아이들이 꽹과리를 들고 마을을 돌았어요.
examples.en: On the festival day, the kids went around the village carrying kkwaenggwari.
Please teach me how to play the kkwaenggwari.

explain: 작고 납작한 쇠 악기로, 채로 쳐서 소리를 내요. 사물놀이에서 가장 높고 날카로운 소리를 내며 연주를 이끌어요. 큰 '징'은 낮고 길게 울려서 소리가 달라요.
explain_en: It is a small, flat metal instrument played by striking it with a mallet. In samulnori it makes the highest, sharpest sound and leads the performance. The large '징' rings low and long, so the sound is different.

examples.en: My younger sibling keeps dodging the work every time we clean.
Stop shirking and help out too.
You shouldn't slack off just because the work is hard.
My friend tried to wriggle out of doing the homework.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 꾀부리는 법이 없어서 다들 좋아해요.
examples.en: He never slacks off, so everybody likes him.
I got scolded by the coach for slacking during practice.

explain: 힘든 일이나 해야 할 일을 요령껏 피하려는 모습에 써요. '게으름 피우다'는 그냥 하기 싫어서 늘어지는 느낌이고, '꾀부리다'는 일부러 피하려는 느낌이 더 있어요. '꾀를 부리다'처럼 '를'을 넣어서도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone cleverly tries to avoid hard work or something they should do. '게으름 피우다' feels like simply being lazy, while '꾀부리다' has more of a sense of deliberately dodging. You can also say '꾀를 부리다' with '를'.

examples.en: His face looks grubby, as if he hasn't washed for days.
That child looked shabby and grimy in his clothes.
I washed my grubby sneakers and made them look new.
The room is so grubby, so let's clean first.

examples.ko: 밤새 일하고 나서 꾀죄죄한 모습으로 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: After working all night, I came home looking scruffy.
The towels got grimy, so I bought new ones.

explain: 사람의 모습이나 옷, 물건이 때가 타고 초라해 보일 때 써요. 그냥 '더럽다'보다 낡고 후줄근한 느낌이 있어요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a person, clothes or things that look dirty and shabby. Compared with plain '더럽다', it has a worn-out, scruffy feel. Saying it directly to a person can be rude.

examples.en: I got angry and crumpled up the letter.

examples.ko: 다 쓴 종이를 꾸겨서 쓰레기통에 던졌어요.
examples.en: I crumpled the used paper and threw it into the trash can.
I wrinkled all my clothes while stuffing them into the bag.
Don't crumple the receipt; keep it flat.
My younger sibling crumpled my test paper and ran away.

examples.ko: 옷을 꾸기면 다림질해도 잘 안 펴져요.
examples.en: If you crumple clothes, they don't smooth out well even when ironed.

explain: 종이나 옷을 주름이 생기게 구기는 동작이에요. 보통 '구기다'라고 하고, '꾸기다'는 그보다 센 느낌의 말이에요. 저절로 주름이 생긴 상태는 '꾸겨지다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the action of crumpling paper or clothes so they get creases. People usually say '구기다', and '꾸기다' is a stronger-sounding form of it. For something that becomes wrinkled by itself, say '꾸겨지다'.

examples.ko: 가방에 오래 넣어 둬서 바지가 꾸깃꾸깃해요.
examples.en: The pants are all wrinkled from being in the bag for so long.
Shops accept even crumpled bills.

examples.ko: 옷이 꾸깃꾸깃해지지 않게 잘 개어 두세요.
examples.en: Fold the clothes well so they don't get wrinkled.
I went to the interview wearing a wrinkled shirt.
The paper got wet in the rain and became crumpled.
I unfolded the crumpled letter and read it.

explain: 주름이 많이 잡혀 구겨진 상태를 나타내서 옷, 종이, 지폐에 자주 써요. 구기는 동작은 '꾸기다', 이미 구겨진 상태는 '꾸깃꾸깃하다'로 말해요. '구깃구깃하다'보다 센 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes a state with many creases, so it fits clothes, paper and banknotes. The action of crumpling is '꾸기다', while the already-crumpled state is '꾸깃꾸깃하다'. It sounds stronger than '구깃구깃하다'.

examples.en: I was hungry, so my stomach made a rumbling sound.

examples.ko: 수업 중에 배에서 꾸르륵 소리가 나서 창피했어요.
examples.en: My stomach growled during class and I was embarrassed.

examples.ko: 꾸르륵 하는 소리가 옆 사람한테까지 들렸어요.
examples.en: The rumbling sound was heard even by the person next to me.

examples.ko: 점심을 걸렀더니 배가 계속 꾸르륵 울려요.
examples.en: I skipped lunch, so my stomach keeps rumbling.

examples.ko: 갑자기 꾸르륵 소리가 나서 모두 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: A sudden rumble came out and everyone looked at me.

examples.ko: 물을 너무 많이 마셨는지 속에서 꾸르륵 소리가 나요.
examples.en: Maybe I drank too much water; my belly is gurgling.

explain: 배 속에서 나는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. '꾸르륵 소리가 나다', '배가 꾸르륵 울리다'처럼 써요. 'ㅗ'로 '꼬르륵'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound from your stomach. You say '꾸르륵 소리가 나다' or '배가 꾸르륵 울리다'. People also say it with 'ㅗ' as '꼬르륵'.

examples.ko: 아침을 안 먹었더니 배가 계속 꾸르륵거려요.
examples.en: I skipped breakfast, so my stomach keeps rumbling.

examples.ko: 속이 꾸르륵거리는 걸 보니 체한 것 같아요.
examples.en: My belly is gurgling, so I think I have indigestion.
My stomach was rumbling, so I went to the restroom.
In the quiet classroom, only my stomach rumbled.

examples.ko: 배가 꾸르륵거리면 따뜻한 물을 마셔 보세요.
examples.en: If your stomach rumbles, try drinking warm water.

examples.ko: 찬 음료를 마시자 뱃속이 꾸르륵거리기 시작했어요.
examples.en: After I drank the cold drink, my belly started to gurgle.

explain: 배고플 때뿐 아니라 소화가 잘 안 되거나 찬 걸 마셨을 때처럼 배 속에서 소리가 날 때도 써요. '배가 꾸르륵거리다' 또는 '배에서 꾸르륵 소리가 나다'로 말해요. 'ㅗ'로 '꼬르륵거리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used not only when you are hungry but any time your belly makes sounds, such as with poor digestion or after a cold drink. You can say '배가 꾸르륵거리다' or '배에서 꾸르륵 소리가 나다'. It can also be said with 'ㅗ' as '꼬르륵거리다'.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에 화단에서 벌레가 꾸물꾸물 기어가요.
examples.en: After the rain, bugs crawl slowly across the flower bed.

examples.ko: 아이가 아침마다 꾸물꾸물 옷을 입어서 늦어요.
examples.en: The child dawdles getting dressed every morning, so we're late.
The caterpillar wriggles slowly on the leaf.

examples.ko: 꾸물꾸물 누워만 있지 말고 빨리 일어나요.
examples.en: Stop lying around sluggishly and get up quickly.
He got up sluggishly and washed his face.
A big snake slithered slowly out of the grass.

explain: '꼬물꼬물'이 작고 귀여운 것의 움직임이라면 '꾸물꾸물'은 좀 더 크고 굼뜬 느낌이에요. 벌레나 뱀이 기어갈 때도, 사람이 일어나거나 준비하는 걸 미루고 늘어질 때도 써요. 동사는 '꾸물대다', '꾸물거리다'예요.
explain_en: Where '꼬물꼬물' is for small, cute movements, '꾸물꾸물' feels bigger and more sluggish. It fits bugs or snakes crawling, and also people dragging their feet about getting up or getting ready. The verbs are '꾸물대다' and '꾸물거리다'.

examples.en: Don't dawdle every morning; get ready quickly.
The bus is coming, so why are you dawdling like this?

examples.ko: 친구랑 수다 떨며 꾸물대다가 기차를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: I lingered chatting with a friend and missed the train.
I saw a bug wriggling on the floor.
A caterpillar is wriggling on the leaf.

examples.ko: 숙제 안 하고 꾸물대면 밤새워야 해요.
examples.en: If you dawdle and don't do your homework, you'll have to stay up all night.

explain: 사람에게 쓰면 '빨리 안 하고 시간을 끈다'는 불만이 담겨서 '꾸물대지 마'처럼 재촉하는 말로 자주 나와요. 벌레에게는 그런 불만 없이 모습만 말해요. 손가락이나 발가락을 조금씩 움직이는 건 '꼼지락대다'라서 달라요.
explain_en: With people it carries a complaint that they are wasting time, so it often shows up as a hurry-up phrase like '꾸물대지 마'. With bugs it just describes the movement, with no complaint. Moving fingers or toes a little at a time is '꼼지락대다', which is different.

examples.en: He always speaks frankly, without pretense.

examples.ko: 꾸밈없이 웃는 모습이 참 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: Her natural, unaffected smile is lovely to see.
You can speak plainly, so please be at ease.

examples.ko: 저는 꾸밈없이 있는 그대로의 모습을 보여 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to show myself just as I am, without putting on airs.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 화장도 안 하고 꾸밈없이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actor appeared natural, without even wearing makeup.
In my diary, I write down my feelings of the day plainly.

explain: 겉으로 꾸미거나 거짓을 보태지 않고 소박하고 솔직하게 하는 모습을 말해요. '솔직히'가 말의 내용에 쓰인다면, '꾸밈없이'는 태도, 모습, 글에도 두루 써요. 형용사 '꾸밈없다'와 '꾸밈없는 사람'처럼도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes being simple and honest, not dressing things up or adding falsehood. '솔직히' mainly concerns what you say, while '꾸밈없이' also fits attitude, appearance and writing. The adjective form '꾸밈없다' is common too, as in '꾸밈없는 사람'.

examples.en: Grandpa's back is bent, so he uses a cane.

examples.ko: 꾸부정한 자세로 오래 앉아 있으면 허리가 아파요.
examples.en: If you sit for long in a hunched posture, your back hurts.
He walks stooped over, so I worry about his health.
Your shoulders are hunched, so try straightening them.

examples.ko: 키 큰 학생이 꾸부정하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The tall student was standing with a stoop.
His back has become hunched as he got older.

explain: 허리, 어깨, 등처럼 몸이 앞으로 약간 굽은 모양을 말해요. 자세가 좋지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 '쭉 펴세요'와 자주 같이 나와요. '구부정하다'와 같은 말인데 더 센 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes the body, such as the back or shoulders, bending slightly forward. It carries a feeling of poor posture, so it often appears with phrases like '쭉 펴세요' (straighten up). It is the same word as '구부정하다' but sounds stronger.

examples.en: The mountain path winds on and on.
The river winds along and flows to the sea.
My younger sibling wrote in wobbly handwriting.
I saw a snake slithering along in curves.

examples.ko: 꾸불꾸불 골목을 따라가면 우리 집이 나와요.
examples.en: If you follow the winding alley, you'll reach my house.
Try drawing a wavy line on the map.

explain: 산길, 강, 뱀처럼 긴 것이 크게 여러 번 휘는 모습에 어울려요. 같은 말의 작은 느낌은 '꼬불꼬불'이라서 좁은 골목이나 가는 선에는 그쪽이 더 자연스러워요. 한 번만 굽은 길에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It suits long things like mountain paths, rivers and snakes that bend widely several times. The smaller-feeling counterpart is '꼬불꼬불', which is more natural for narrow alleys and thin lines. It isn't used for a path that bends only once.

examples.ko: 이 길은 너무 꾸불꾸불해서 멀미가 나요.
examples.en: This road is so winding that I get carsick.
I passed through the winding alleys and arrived at the market.
The handwriting is so squiggly that it's hard to read.
The way the river winds along is beautiful.
My hair is wavy, so I straighten it every morning.
The mountain road is winding, so drive carefully.

explain: 주로 길, 강 같은 큰 것이 여러 번 휘어 있을 때 쓰고, 멀미가 나거나 운전 조심하라는 말과 자주 이어져요. 글씨나 머리카락이 고르지 않게 휘었을 때도 써요. 작고 가는 것에는 '꼬불꼬불하다'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for big things like roads and rivers with many bends, and often goes with remarks about carsickness or careful driving. It also describes uneven, wavy handwriting or hair. For small, thin things, '꼬불꼬불하다' fits better.

examples.en: I came home late and got scolded by my mother.
The teacher smiled and gently advised us instead of scolding.

examples.ko: 숙제를 안 해서 꾸지람을 들을까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried I'll be scolded for not doing my homework.

examples.ko: 아이에게 꾸지람만 하지 말고 칭찬도 해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just scold the child; praise him too.
My younger sibling burst into tears at Dad's scolding.

examples.ko: 꾸지람을 듣고도 그는 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: Even after being scolded, he didn't say anything.

explain: 부모나 선생님처럼 윗사람이 아랫사람의 잘못을 나무랄 때 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '꾸지람을 듣다', '꾸지람을 하다'로 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '꾸중', '야단'이 있고, 일상 대화에서는 '혼나다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when someone senior, such as a parent or teacher, scolds a junior for a mistake. You usually say '꾸지람을 듣다' or '꾸지람을 하다'. Similar words are '꾸중' and '야단', and in daily talk people often say '혼나다'.

examples.ko: 할머니가 부엌 선반에 꿀단지를 올려 두셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma put the honey jar on the kitchen shelf.

examples.ko: 꿀단지에 숟가락을 넣어 꿀을 한 숟갈 떠요.
examples.en: I put a spoon into the honey jar and scoop out a spoonful.

examples.ko: 만화 속 곰이 꿀단지를 보고 좋아했어요.
examples.en: The bear in the cartoon was delighted to see the honey jar.

examples.ko: 꿀단지 뚜껑을 꼭 닫아야 개미가 안 들어가요.
examples.en: You must close the honey jar lid tightly so ants don't get in.
I received a big jar of honey as a gift from the countryside.

examples.ko: 꿀단지가 비어서 새 꿀을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: The honey jar was empty, so I bought new honey.

explain: '단지'는 입구가 넓고 배가 불룩한 그릇이라서 꿀뿐 아니라 '김치 단지', '된장 단지'처럼도 써요. 동화나 만화에서 곰이 좋아하는 물건으로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A '단지' is a pot with a wide mouth and a round belly, so it is used for honey but also in '김치 단지' and '된장 단지'. It often appears in stories and cartoons as something bears love.

examples.ko: 쓴 약을 물 없이 꿀떡 삼켰어요.
examples.en: I swallowed the bitter medicine in one gulp without water.
My younger sibling gulped down the snack.

examples.ko: 시원한 주스를 꿀떡 마시고 다시 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I downed the cold juice in one go and ran again.
I gulped down my saliva and opened my mouth.

examples.ko: 맛있는 음식을 보자 침이 꿀떡 넘어갔어요.
examples.en: When I saw the delicious food, my mouth watered and I swallowed.
The baby swallowed the baby food in one go.

explain: 음식, 물, 침, 약을 한 번에 삼키는 모양과 소리를 나타내요. '꿀꺽'도 비슷하게 쓰고, '꿀떡 삼키다'처럼 '삼키다'와 자주 같이 나와요. '꿀떡'이라는 떡 이름도 따로 있으니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It describes the manner and sound of swallowing food, water, saliva or medicine in one go. '꿀꺽' is used in a similar way, and it often pairs with '삼키다', as in '꿀떡 삼키다'. There is also a rice cake called '꿀떡', so don't confuse them.

en: being in one's sleep; being while dreaming

examples.ko: 꿈결에 어머니 목소리를 들은 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I heard my mother's voice in my sleep.

examples.ko: 여행 첫날은 정말 꿈결 같은 하루였어요.
examples.en: The first day of the trip was a truly dreamlike day.
I was sleepy, so the teacher's words sounded like they came from a dream.

examples.ko: 꿈결에 누가 문을 두드리는 소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: Half asleep, I heard someone knocking on the door.
I can't tell whether this is a dream or reality.
The baby smiled and waved its hand in its sleep.

explain: '꿈결에'는 자면서 꿈을 꾸는 중이거나 잠이 든 듯 만 듯 흐릿한 때를 말해요. '꿈속'이 꿈 안의 장소라면, '꿈결'은 꿈처럼 흐릿한 상태나 때를 가리켜요. '꿈결 같다'는 현실 같지 않게 아름답고 행복한 시간을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: '꿈결에' refers to the time you are dreaming, or the hazy moment when you are barely asleep. While '꿈속' is the place inside a dream, '꿈결' points to a dreamlike, blurry state or moment. '꿈결 같다' is used for a time so beautiful or happy that it feels unreal.
